analysis:
Only docs/developer/test.md changed: the 'Last updated' date, plus a rewritten description of scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py and the dev-branch release lane (.github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml) at roughly head lines 1048-1059. A second hunk in head lines 1066-1078 appears to be mostly unchanged text shifted by the insertion. This is a documentation-only change with no runtime code, so no new attack surface or regression is introduced by the PR itself.

The new text claims the lane is push-to-dev only, with no dispatch, no input and no ref:. It also claims the caller uses environment: dev and secrets: inherit, and that release-provider.yml reads only DEV_* secrets or the five Apple signing secrets, only in the signing job, with Developer ID signing, notarization and no ad-hoc signing. It describes the guard test, not the workflow source, so these claims cannot be verified from the supplied evidence.

Open questions for later review: the actual release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that `secrets: inherit` really limits exposure to DEV_* and Apple signing secrets. Nor can I confirm that a push to dev, which a branch writer can trigger, cannot reach production signing or A-005, A-011 and A-017 registration. The earlier text said 'no signing identity or secret', so the new text widens the dev lane's documented authority to include Apple Developer ID signing secrets. That is a real change in the documented trust of the dev lane, but it only matters if the workflow actually does this. The threat model has no TB or T entry for the release pipeline, and the supplied threats (T-013, T-034, T-054) concern provider binary identity and qualification. Any workflow change belongs in a pass that sees the workflow files. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by the documentation text alone.
